findings.claim: The taskId route parameter has no validation pipe before being inserted into the Rhinestone status URL, so a crafted value containing path traversal or a decoded '?' can redirect the credentialed request (sent with the project-wide x-api-key header) to an arbitrary path on the Rhinestone host, since the route itself has no auth guard.
The upstream error message is passed back to the caller unchanged, so an attacker exploiting the unvalidated taskId can see part of the response from whatever Rhinestone path they reached.

This relayer forwards safeTxHash to Rhinestone without checking it, even though Rhinestone documents the field as required for execTransaction and to be omitted for multiSend/deployments, so requests can reach Rhinestone missing a hash it needs or carrying a hash that doesn't match the calldata.
This relayer likewise forwards safeTxHash without validating or requiring it for execTransaction or stripping it for multiSend/deployment calls, unlike RelayFeeRelayer which does enforce this.

Rhinestone's status field is passed through unmapped even though the public DTO still documents Gelato's status codes (100/110/200/400/500); if Rhinestone uses different codes, clients polling status would be silently misled.
No test sends safeTxHash on the daily-limit or no-fee-campaign chains or asserts it in the outgoing request body, and neither relayer has a unit spec, so the missing validation behavior is untested.

RELAY_PROVIDER_API_KEY is introduced as a new required configuration variable while the previous 12 per-chain keys were removed, so production deployment will fail to boot if this variable is not provisioned beforehand.
getTaskStatus no longer checks chainId at all, because the removed per-chain key lookup previously served as that check, so this validation was lost in the change.
The blockHash, blockNumber, gasUsed and createdAt fields were made optional but are never set anywhere in the code, so they should be removed rather than left as unused optional fields.
formatError logs the full upstream response body, which may echo back request data, so only the status and message should be logged instead.
